subject.title: A fast vector search silently leaves neighbors behind

capsule.title: A fast vector search silently leaves neighbors behind
capsule.summary: At efSearch 10, HNSW appears extremely fast but recall@10 is only 0.949. Reporting QPS alone turns missing neighbors into invisible success.
capsule.trigger: Search 10,000 SIFT-128 vectors with a deliberately narrow candidate frontier and compare against exact brute-force ground truth.
capsule.observed: The index reaches 105,741 QPS at 0.949 recall; increasing efSearch to 32 lowers QPS to 45,149 and raises recall to 0.997.
capsule.invariant: Approximate-search latency is interpretable only beside exact-ground-truth recall at the same k and dataset.
capsule.fix: Publish the full recall-latency frontier, test monotonic recall under increasing efSearch, and select budgets from target recall.

timeline.title: Narrow the candidate frontier
timeline.detail: efSearch 10 explores very few graph nodes and minimizes work per query.

timeline.title: Win the latency chart
timeline.detail: Throughput rises while approximately five percent of the true neighbors disappear.

timeline.title: Ask exact search
timeline.detail: Brute-force labels expose every omitted neighbor and produce recall@10.

timeline.title: Publish the Pareto curve
timeline.detail: No QPS claim is accepted without its recall operating point.

limits: The published absolute QPS uses 10,000 in-memory vectors on an M-series CPU, not a million-vector production index.
